labels.epicDescription: Epic: a large task with subtasks

comments.closedByPr: Closed by PR {prs}: GitHub didn't link the PR to the task

actualize.lead: {task} #{number} ({epicWord} #{epic}): epic refresh after the merge — bring the epic's open tasks in line with what shipped.
actualize.fetch: The whole assignment — the texts of the epic's open tasks, the PR files, what the script named, the checks by meaning — is printed by `{command}`: run it first, outside the sandbox (gh doesn't work in it); don't collect the tasks and the PR yourself.
actualize.openTasks: ## The epic's open tasks — its sub-issues, not a list in the epic's description
actualize.copies: ## Copies of links in text — remove them: GitHub keeps the links (sub-issue, blocked by)
actualize.answers: ## Answers to open questions in comments — check that it answers that question and move it into «{questions}» (✅ and the answer at the question, same numbering); if not — leave it
actualize.checks: ## Checks by meaning — yours (canon — reference.md of the github skill, «Epic refresh on task close»); the mechanics — blocked by on done tasks, the questions label without open questions, milestones without open tasks — the script did
actualize.scope: You change only GitHub tasks — description, «{questions}», links, status; the github skill script — `{script}`: not done — `task drop <N>`, a new one — `task new … --branch-type <type> --epic {epic}` (it sets the estimate itself); an answer at a question — `task answer <N> <k> "<answer>"`. Don't touch code, branches or git; don't close #{number}, epic #{epic} or their milestones — task close does that after you.
actualize.comment: What you fixed — one line in a comment on epic #{epic} (`gh issue comment {epic} --repo {repo}`); nothing to fix — no comment.
actualize.answer: Answer — fixes one per line with task numbers and questions to the owner, if any; otherwise «The block is current».
actualize.milestone: milestone «{title}» closed — no open tasks in it

queue.prompt: {task} #{number} in {repo}{epic}: you are an executor of the dispatcher session. The whole assignment is printed by `{command}` — call it first, outside the sandbox (gh doesn't work in it).
queue.lead: {task} #{number} «{title}» in {repo}{epic}: you are an executor of the dispatcher session — do the task whole by the canon, like a session in auto mode: the task's questions, `{script} task status {number} "{inProgress}" --branch <type>/{number}-<slug>`, the branch from a fresh origin/main, code and tests, PR, green CI, `pr premerge`, merge, deploy, the epic refresh, `{script} task close {number}`.
queue.resume: The task is already «{inProgress}» and has a branch {branches} — a restart: continue its work. The branch is checked out in another worktree (`git worktree list`) — work in that one, not in your new one: in Claude Code — `EnterWorktree` with its path; uncommitted work — `git status` there. In no worktree — check it out in yours.
queue.subagent: You are a subagent, not a session:
queue.session: - don't rename or archive the session and don't write the last line («{done}») — the dispatcher does;
queue.wait: - wait for CI and the deploy with a regular call, not in the background: a background command doesn't wake a subagent, and a Bash call lives up to 10 minutes — `{waitCi} pr <PR> --timeout 540` (after the merge — `merged <PR>`), on TIMEOUT — the same call again;
queue.git: - git — in separate calls, without `cd`, `&&` and `|`: worktree isolation refuses a compound command with git;
queue.subagents: - writing subagents — launch as needed, no limit: each gets its own worktree and «{task} #{number}» at the start of its prompt (`est` links its work by it); bring their commits into your branch, remove their worktrees and branches yourself after the merge — what didn't go, name in the answer;
queue.found: - work found outside the task — `{script} task new …` (work of the task's epic — with `--epic`: the dispatcher picks it up), without a chip — name it in the answer;
queue.question: - a question without a clear recommendation — into «{questions}» of the task; don't start the code that depends on it and answer the dispatcher: the owner's answer comes back here.
queue.answer: The answer to the dispatcher — one line: `merged #<PR>` · `question: <the question, options, recommendation>` · `failed: <what stopped and where>`.
